findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py as a consumer that must be updated for the new defaults (24/160) and clamp (960), not just add new formula tests.
evidence: test_completion_budget.py:53-60 hard-codes 8/48 defaults and `verify_step_floor(100, vc) == _VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX == 480`
test_completion_budget.py:71,77 assert `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS == 250` and `captured['max_iterations'] == 48` (verify_step_floor(1))
This test lives outside completion.py's directory (tests/interfaces/contracts/) — an unenumerated consumer of the changed constants
findings.finding: AC1 raises the defaults (8->24, 48->160) and the clamp (480->960) but does not enumerate the existing consumer test tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py, which hard-codes the current values and will fail: it asserts verify_step_floor(1)==48, verify_step_floor(8)==64, verify_step_floor(40)==320, verify_step_floor(100)==_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX==480, and captured max_iterations==48. These break under the new defaults/clamp.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria line 1 ('Defaults raised (24 / 160; clamp 960) ... unit tests on the formula')
scenarios: `make lint`/test run after the default+clamp change: the existing contract tests fail on the stale 48/64/320/480 expectations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1: update the existing test_completion_budget.py assertions (verify_step_floor values and the _VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX==480 pin) to the new 24/160/960 mechanics alongside the new evidence-surface tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the empty-own-file_impact fingerprint for parent/epic tickets via the subtree/child impact set (or child signatures) rather than the whole-tree sha, so unrelated commits do not defeat cross-run reuse on the multi-AC epics the plan targets; test that an unrelated commit does not invalidate an epic entry when own file_impact is empty.
evidence: Plan rejects whole-tree sha: 'any unrelated commit would rotate it and defeat reuse'

Plan's primary evidence for the cache is epic re-verify cost; epics/parents are containers that commonly declare no OWN file_impact (completion_prefetch.py distinguishes root's own vs children's declared impact)
completion_prefetch.py:259 confirms containers rely on child-declared impact rather than own paths
findings.finding: The empty-file_impact fallback to the whole-tree sha reinstates the invalidation behavior the plan itself rejects as defeating reuse, and epics/containers frequently have empty OWN file_impact, so the highest-value reuse targets land in the defeated path.
findings.location: Plan section 3: 'falling back to the whole-tree sha only when file_impact is empty'
scenarios: A 15-AC epic with empty own file_impact: every unrelated commit rotates the whole-tree sha and invalidates all cached PASS verdicts, so cross-run convergence never happens for the very case the plan cites
findings.suggested_fix: When own file_impact is empty but the ticket has children, derive the scoped fingerprint from the union of direct-child file_impact blobs (via _subtree_impacts) instead of the whole-tree sha; reserve the whole-tree fallback for genuinely childless tickets with empty file_impact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how seeded cached-PASS records satisfy or bypass the finalizer's met:false-on-missing-evidence rule (completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-25): either seed a finalizer-satisfying evidence/citation payload, or give the finalizer an explicit 'credited/pre-proven record — echo as met:true, do not re-evaluate' instruction co-located in the prompt.
evidence: Plan: '…the tool-free finalizer (completion_verifier_finalizer.md:14-32…) sees ordinary banked records — the existing echo + merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamp seam is unchanged.'

Finalizer prompt lines 23-25: 'Set met: true only when the corresponding evidence demonstrates the whole criterion. Missing, incomplete, contradictory, or truncated evidence is not enough and must be met: false.'
Finalizer prompt lines 29-30: 'Copy only citations actually present in the evidence. Never invent a path, line number, URL, identifier, or source.'
CriterionBank entries carry an 'evidence' text field (completion_banking.py:455) that the finalizer echoes; the plan does not state what evidence text a seeded cache entry supplies.
findings.finding: The plan seeds cross-run cached PASS verdicts into the run-scoped CriterionBank as 'ordinary banked records' and asserts the tool-free finalizer's echo + re-stamp seam is unchanged, but the finalizer prompt's decision rule (completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-25: 'Missing, incomplete, contradictory, or truncated evidence is not enough and must be met:false' and 'Copy only citations actually present in the evidence. Never invent') will re-judge a seeded record to met:false whenever its evidence/citation text is absent or stale — silently flipping a credited PASS to FAIL. The plan never specifies what evidence a seeded cache entry carries, nor how the finalizer distinguishes a pre-proven credited record it must honor from one it re-evaluates.
scenarios: A re-verify credits a cached PASS whose stored evidence text is empty or references a now-moved line; the finalizer applies its 'incomplete/missing evidence -> met:false' rule and returns FAIL for a criterion the plan intended to credit.

AC-3's 'credits still-valid cached PASS verdicts… and spends budget only on unproven criteria' is asserted but the finalizer may re-flip the credited PASS, so convergence across runs is not actually achieved.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the 'source' provenance value for cache-seeded CriterionBank records (e.g. source='cache') and state its overwrite/re-stamp behavior in harvest_structured_into_bank and merge_finalizer_with_bank relative to tool/harvest/fallback entries.
evidence: upsert signature stamps source (completion_banking.py:442) with call sites source='tool' (:556) and source='harvest' (:589); 1d71 adds a fallback source.
Plan: seeded cache entries become 'pre-banked records' but the plan names no source value for them.
harvest_structured_into_bank preserves/overwrites based on prior-entry provenance/marker (per 1d71 comment), so an undefined seeded source affects overwrite semantics.
findings.finding: Seeded cross-run-cache records are written into the CriterionBank whose entries stamp a 'source' provenance value, but the plan does not define a source value for cache-seeded records against the existing vocabulary (tool/harvest, plus fallback per 1d71). Downstream banking/harvest/re-stamp logic keys on record provenance, and an undefined source value for seeded entries leaves their handling (e.g. preserve-vs-overwrite on re-harvest, marker re-stamp) unspecified.
scenarios: A successor run re-harvests over a seeded cache record; without a defined source, whether the seeded PASS is preserved or overwritten is unspecified.
merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps from the bank; a seeded record with an unrecognized/absent source could be mis-handled by provenance-keyed branches.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State concrete numeric defaults for child_traversal (steps per direct child) and fixed_overhead in step 2, grounded in the observed 5-10 requests/child cost.
evidence: 'budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children (epics/parents) + fixed_overhead'
per_criterion is given (24) and floor_min (160) but child_traversal and fixed_overhead coefficients are unspecified
Current-mechanics note cites '5-10 requests each' for child reads but does not convert this into a chosen coefficient
findings.finding: The evidence-surface formula names `child_traversal` and `fixed_overhead` terms but never states their numeric values, leaving the executor to choose them.
findings.location: Plan step 2 + AC 'Budget sizing adds a child-traversal term'
scenarios: Executor picks child_traversal=1 vs 10, producing wildly different budgets; the 'childful sizes strictly larger' AC passes either way but the intended generosity is undefined
findings.suggested_fix: e.g. child_traversal=16 steps/child (≈8 requests, matching observed 5-10) and fixed_overhead=16 steps for initial show_ticket + description parse; add a unit test asserting these produce the intended epic sizes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a RETIRE/cleanup path for the completion_verdicts cache (e.g. prune entries whose scoped fingerprint no longer matches on seed, or a TTL/max-entries-per-ticket bound).
evidence: 'A separate cache at `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json`, written ONLY on a validated PASS record'
No TTL, eviction, or cleanup mechanism is described
Invalidation is by non-match (scoped fingerprint/text change) which leaves the superseded file on disk
findings.finding: The new ticket-scoped verdict cache has no RETIRE/cleanup path; entries accumulate under `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/` and stale-fingerprint entries are never removed, only stop matching.
scenarios: A ticket re-verified many times across churning file_impact blobs accumulates orphan JSON files indefinitely across the repo's .rebar cache
findings.suggested_fix: On seed at run start, delete cache files for a criterion-hash whose stored fingerprint mismatches the current scoped fingerprint (write-through eviction), so only live entries persist.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the cache's scoped fingerprint for parent/epic tickets to include child-ticket state (child closure/certification signatures and/or child file_impact blobs), so a child reopen/decertify/rework invalidates the parent's cached PASS; add a RED->GREEN test where a child changes but the parent's own file_impact is untouched.
evidence: Plan: 'key each entry by (criterion-text hash, scoped material fingerprint) where the scoped fingerprint ... narrowed to the blobs under the ticket's file_impact paths'
Problem defect 1: epic criteria 'traverse child tickets (show_ticket + comments + repo reads)' — evidence surface is the subtree, not the parent's own blobs
completion_prefetch.py:259 '_subtree_impacts ... The root's own file_impact is NOT counted here' — containers carry child-declared impact
completion.py:110-130 child_closure_findings: an epic's certifiability hinges on child closure/certified state, which the parent's file_impact blobs do not fingerprint
findings.finding: The cross-run cache's scoped fingerprint (blobs under the ticket's OWN file_impact paths) does not cover child-ticket state, yet epic criteria depend on child closure/certification/child file_impact; a reopened or decertified child would not rotate the parent's fingerprint, crediting a stale PASS on re-verify.
findings.location: Plan section 3 (Cross-run PASS-verdict cache) and AC line 'an unrelated commit outside file_impact does NOT invalidate'
scenarios: Epic AC 'all child stories closed & certified' cached PASS; a child is later reopened/re-worked/decertified; parent re-verify credits the stale PASS because the parent's own file_impact blobs are unchanged
findings.suggested_fix: For tickets with direct children, fold the direct children's certified-closure signatures (or the subtree file_impact blob set from _subtree_impacts) into the scoped fingerprint alongside the parent's own file_impact blobs, so child-state changes rotate the key.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether child_traversal / fixed_overhead are hardcoded constants (preferred, no evidenced tuning need) or new config keys; if config keys, justify the operator-tuning requirement given the existing two verify.* scaling params already cover the primary levers.
evidence: Plan: 'budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children (epics/parents) + fixed_overhead'
search: child_traversal and fixed_overhead have zero codebase hits — both are new
_config_schema.py:249-250 shows the two existing scaling params are BOTH config keys; adding two more would extend that surface
Absence rationale: the plan gives values/tuning need for neither new coefficient, so the case for making them operator-tunable config is unestablished
findings.finding: The evidence-surface scaling formula introduces two new coefficients (child_traversal, fixed_overhead) that do not exist in the codebase, but the plan does not state whether they land as new config keys or hardcoded constants. The existing sibling params (completion_verify_steps_per_criterion, completion_verify_step_floor_min) are both config keys, so mirroring that pattern would add two more config keys — config-surface proliferation for coefficients with no evidenced need for operator tuning.
findings.location: Plan point 2 (Evidence-surface-aware scaling) and AC line 2
scenarios: Author defaults to adding child_traversal/fixed_overhead as verify.* config keys by pattern-matching the existing two, growing the config surface with untunable knobs
findings.suggested_fix: Land child_traversal and fixed_overhead as module-level constants documented at verify_step_floor, reserving config keys only for the two existing primary levers unless a tuning need is demonstrated.

relation_snapshot.py:343-345: current_material_fingerprint_impl '...from a LIGHT read (the ticket + its child ids only — no full child fetch, no LLM)'
attest.py:671-677: current_material_fingerprint delegates to current_material_fingerprint_impl; material derives from description/child-ids, not file_impact blobs
search: no 'file_impact' reference in completion_banking.py
findings.finding: The load-bearing invalidation premise mischaracterizes the existing fingerprint seam: the plan claims the scoped fingerprint 'reuses the existing BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps seam... narrowed to the blobs under the ticket's file_impact paths', but resolve_bank_stamps (completion_banking.py:335-355) resolves material via current_material_fingerprint -> material_fingerprint, which fingerprints the ticket's DESCRIPTION + child ids from a light ticket read (relation_snapshot.py:343-363, 'the ticket + its child ids only'), NOT repo file blobs under file_impact paths. There is no file_impact-scoped blob fingerprint in this seam to narrow.
scenarios: Implementer treats the file_impact-blob fingerprint as an existing capability to reuse and under-scopes the new work of computing blob hashes under file_impact paths

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the capability assertion in AC3: state explicitly that per-file_impact-path blob fingerprinting is a NEW computation (not a behavior resolve_bank_stamps/_resolve_tree_sha provides today), and specify which git object state it hashes (HEAD blobs vs working tree vs index) so the invalidation key is well-defined.
evidence: Plan: 'the scoped fingerprint reuses the existing BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps seam (:358-392) narrowed to the blobs under the ticket's file_impact paths, falling back to the whole-tree sha only when file_impact is empty'
completion_banking.py:335-355 resolve_bank_stamps: material_fingerprint = current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id, ...) — ticket material, not per-path file blobs
completion_banking.py:358-373 _resolve_tree_sha: `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` — whole committed tree sha, not path-scoped blobs
The narrowing-to-file_impact-blobs behavior is not present in the cited seam; it is a new fingerprinting computation.
findings.finding: AC3 asserts the scoped material fingerprint 'reuses the existing BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps seam narrowed to the blobs under the ticket's file_impact paths', but neither existing stamp currently computes per-path blob content: resolve_bank_stamps derives material_fingerprint from current_material_fingerprint (ticket description/children/file_impact list — not file-content blobs) and tree_sha from the whole-tree HEAD (_resolve_tree_sha). Narrowing to per-file_impact-path blob hashes is a NEW capability presented as a reuse, so the 'reuse' claim is unverified.
scenarios: Implementer discovers resolve_bank_stamps yields ticket-material/whole-tree stamps and must build a new per-path blob-hashing routine rather than 'narrowing' an existing one, changing the scope/effort estimate.
If the new blob-scoped fingerprint is under-specified (e.g. which git object: staged vs HEAD vs working tree), invalidation could miss an in-flight change and credit a stale PASS.
